title: Her view of Joe's religious music and his illness
summary: She regrets that Joe left jazz and calls his religious commitment fanatical but sincere, and mentions a past serious illness.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Does he write religious music now?
He does. Yes, he does. This is what he's involved in. He's involved in religious, and he seems to get satisfaction out of doing that, you know.
There are some people making money recording religious music.

Well, this is true. I can't say that this is true about my brother, however. I wish it was. I would like to see him, you know, do something, where he was going to make a good living at it, because he's a good guy and he is a talented man, but I think he's like some people who when they get into a religious thing they get a little -- I have to say fanatical. I call it fanatical, and this is not a

criticism at all. But I think many times with some people you have an ability, you have a talent, and I think you might look at things in a little different way, in a way that it doesn't benefit you. I think that's what a talent is all about, really. I think when God has given one ability and talent, it's given to you for your use and for you to help yourself and to be able to help your fellow man. So I just hope -- I hope that some day he will be able to -- he's tried awfully hard to get into various fields, you know, in religions. But he just doesn't want to look the other way at all, and this is really -- what I'm trying to say is this is where it is with him. This is where it is. This is where he got his -- just like me getting my -- I got my recognition in jazz, you know, and I just -- I couldn't see myself getting into anything, into another phase of music. And this is not a putdown at all. But I started out playing religious music, you know, but the religious music was sort of closely associated, in a way, the type of music that we did in the church was closely associated with it, so it was no problem.
But anyway, that's the way it goes, as I say, with some people, and my brother is -- he's living up to his conviction.
Is he still here in Los Angeles?
Yes, he is. Yes, he's very active in the Seventh Day Adventist Church.
It's been a long, long time since I've seen him.

Yeah, and he's very well liked. One time he was ill. He had a very serious illness, oh, several years ago. Joe was very, very ill at that time. We thought we would lose him, and thank God he snapped out of it. He takes care of himself. He looks wonderful.
